title: Dedicated Elastic Reservation Contracts and Emergency Fill (PRD)
creator: Maya Chen
description: This PRD defines Elastic Reservation Contracts (ERCs) for Dedicated capacity: per-tenant, timeboxable reservation profiles that allow negotiated headroom, automated emergency fill, and transparent accounting. ERCs unify reserved pools, soft-burst behavior, and emergency-fill credits into a contractual surface that teams can adopt to reduce costly manual arbitration during spikes and to provide predictable SLOs for tenants.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity want predictability (latency SLOs and throughput) while avoiding paying for large, idle headroom. Current reserved-pool semantics are rigid: either fixed reservation or opportunistic best-effort burst. On incidents or coordinated spikes, tenants experience noisy neighbor eviction or manual capacity handoffs. Engineering has built preliminary autoscale hooks and a credit ledger prototype but lacks a product contract and rollout plan that balances economics and reliability.
goals: 1) Define ERC product surface and user contract (terms, headroom %, refill cadence). 2) Implement emergency-fill orchestration with bounded impact on other tenants. 3) Provide transparent accounting and UI/CLI for ERC state and credit balance. 4) Integrate ERCs with autoscaler and prewarm mechanisms to reduce cold-start latency for emergency allocations.
non_goals: 1) Replace existing permanent reserved pools; ERCs are optional add-on. 2) Provide full legal contract templates for enterprise procurement (product will provide standard operational terms only). 3) Implement model-level fine-grained kernel tuning—this PRD focuses on allocation, routing, and accounting layers.
requirements: REQ-1: ERC creation API: tenant can create an ERC with parameters: baseline_reservation (vCPU/GPU units), headroom_pct (0-100), max_emergency_fill (units), refill_policy (time-window or credit-based), and priority_tier.
REQ-2: Headroom negotiation: system validates ERC against cluster capacity and suggests default headroom based on historical 95th-percentile usage for the tenant over the last 7 days.
REQ-3: Emergency-fill orchestration: when tenant usage exceeds baseline+headroom, automatically allocate emergency_fill up to max_emergency_fill if cluster-wide safety budget permits.

REQ-4: Safety budget and fairness: emergency-fill consumes a global safety_budget ledger with per-zone accounting; allocations are throttled when cluster safety_budget < threshold and fallback policies (deny / degrade to lower-tier model) are applied.
REQ-5: Credit ledger and reconciliation: ERCs track credits consumed and replenished per refill_policy; operators can audit ledger and tenants can query their balance via API and Console.
REQ-6: Observability: emit ERC lifecycle events, emergency-fill events, prewarm triggers, and credit changes to telemetry backends with tenant, cluster, and zone tags.
REQ-7: Console UX: add ERC management page showing active contracts, headroom utilization heatmap, credit balance, and recent emergency-fill events with timestamps and durations.
REQ-8: RBAC & audit: ERC operations (create/update/terminate) require appropriate permissions; all actions must generate immutable audit logs for Private deployments.

REQ-9: Rollback & graceful expiry: when an ERC is terminated, emergency allocations should be drained within a configurable grace window (default 10 minutes) with optional tenant notification webhooks.
REQ-10: Integration with autoscaler and prewarm: emergency-fill triggers should optionally request prewarm on the target nodes or pin warm replicas to reduce latency spikes.
REQ-11: Billing & metering: produce per-tenant usage reports that differentiate baseline reserved usage, headroom consumed, and emergency-fill charges for invoicing.
REQ-12: Test harness: create simulator to run synthetic spike scenarios verifying fairness, safety budget exhaustion, and recovery behavior.
REQ-13: Backwards compatibility: tenants without ERCs should continue to operate under existing reserved-pool semantics unchanged.
REQ-14: Documentation and SDKs: provide API reference, Console walkthrough, and SDK helpers for creating/monitoring ERCs in Python and Typescript.
REQ-15: Performance envelope: emergency-fill allocation decision must complete within 200ms for 95% of requests in normal control-plane load.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: ERC API can create/update/delete contracts; sample ERC created in staging and returned expected suggested headroom based on last-7-day usage.

AC-2: In a controlled spike test (tenant usage ramps to 3x baseline), emergency-fill allocated up to configured max_emergency_fill and reduced tail-p99 latency by at least 30% compared to no-emergency-fill baseline.

AC-3: Global safety_budget enforcement: when safety_budget is set to 20% of cluster free capacity, emergency-fill attempts exceeding budget are denied and logged; denial path triggers fallback policy and emits an alert to oncall.
AC-4: Credit ledger reconciliation shows correct debits/credits after three refill cycles and matches simulated billing report within 0.5% tolerance.
AC-5: Console shows ERC state with correct headroom utilization visualization and last emergency-fill event details in staging for test tenant.
AC-6: RBAC: users without ERC_write permission receive 403 on create/update attempts; audit logs include user, action, timestamp, and resulting contract id.
AC-7: Prewarm integration reduces median cold-start tokens latency by measurable amount in emergency-fill path in end-to-end test.
AC-8: Load test: control-plane decision latency for emergency allocation stays under 200ms p95 across simulated 1000 concurrent allocation requests.
AC-9: Documentation pages and SDK samples published in the docs site and linked from Console before public beta launch.
AC-10: Security scan completed and no high-severity findings related to ERC endpoints; operator-approved checklist signed off.
success_metrics: SM-1: Reduction in manual capacity handoffs: target 80% decrease in engineering-initiated manual reassignments for tenants adopting ERCs within first 3 months.
SM-2: Latency stability for ERC tenants: p99 tail latency for default gen endpoints remains within SLA 99.9% of time during spikes in first quarter after rollout.
SM-3: Adoption: 25% of new Dedicated customers opt into ERCs within 60 days of GA launch.
SM-4: Cost predictability: invoices for ERC-adopting tenants show less than 10% variance month-over-month in committed categories.
SM-5: Emergency-fill fairness: no single tenant consumes more than 30% of global safety_budget over rolling 24h window in production tests.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal alpha): API + simulator + console mock; limited to infra and solutions teams. Phase 2 (private beta): select 3 pilot tenants with dedicated support, enable read-only ledger and soft-emergency-fill mode. Phase 3 (public beta): enable full ERC semantics and billing reports for new Dedicated purchases. Phase 4 (GA): enable migration tooling for existing reserved pools and provide opt-in telemetry summaries for historical usage.
monitoring_and_telemetry: Emit metrics: erc_creations, erc_deletes, emergency_fill_requests, emergency_fill_denials, safety_budget_level, headroom_utilization_pct, credit_debits, credit_replenishments. Dashboards: ERC Overview, Safety Budget Heatmap, Per-tenant ERC Activity. Alerting: emergency_fill_denial_rate > 1/min for 5m, safety_budget < 5% per-zone, unexpected credit reconciliation errors.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Emergency-fill could be gamed by tenants to bypass cost controls. Mitigation: enforce max_emergency_fill, require billing admission tests, and include damping factors on repeated requests.

Risk: Safety budget exhaustion causing widespread denials. Mitigation: conservative default budgets, graceful degradation policies (lower-tier model fallback), and operator override capability with audit trail.
Risk: Complexity in billing reconciliation. Mitigation: build reconciliation simulator, run cross-team dry-runs before billing integration, provide detailed line-item exports for tenants.
Risk: Increased control-plane latency under load. Mitigation: lightweight allocation decisions, backpressure, and circuit-breaker that falls back to baseline routing if control-plane overloaded.
Risk: Confusing UX leading to misconfigured ERCs. Mitigation: provide guided defaults, validation warnings, and a staging validation sandbox for tenants to preview ERC effects.
notes: This PRD intentionally avoids specifying low-level kernel behavior; runtime team will provide an implementation contract for emergency allocation tokens. Expect several follow-up tickets for UX flows and billing schema changes. Coordinate with legal for any customer-facing contract language after private beta.
